clean.tx: u’i ke wira’i ta ke u ‘u ym
clean.tl: Wira’i folk didn’t eat any manioc meal.

clean.tx: ma’e ke kaitã ta kekar a’e ta o ho, te’õru namõ kaitã ta
clean.tl: Caetano folks went hunting, Te’õru also.

clean.tx: kaitã ta
clean.tl: Caetano folks

clean.tx: nde kurumĩ ta rehe hũ ere xo my
clean.tl: Why do you want young boys?

clean.tx: karai ta u ‘u katu tĩ
clean.tl: Non-Indians eat it also.

clean.tx: pe i mu o ho i ngi
clean.tl: then his brother went away from him

clean.tx: jakare ke kaitã japi amõ tĩ
clean.tl: Caetano also shot an alligator

clean.tx: pe jande ja jan x oty
clean.tl: then we ran towards him

clean.tx: ihẽ ke a'e mu'e tĩ
clean.tl: he also taught me

clean.tx: a
clean.tl: I

clean.tx: ja
clean.tl: we

clean.tx: ihē
clean.tl: I

clean.tx: ìhẽ pe me'ẽ we mi amõ
clean.tl: He gave me a tiny piece.

clean.tx: jawar ta pe nahã upa ngã me'ẽ my
clean.tl: Perhaps they gave it all to the dogs.

clean.tx: upa xuã pe ihẽ amondo
clean.tl: I sent everything to João.

clean.tx: aʔi ɪmanhaɾkɛ kuɾumĩ ɾɛhɛ pɪnu iʃɔ
clean.tl: A long time ago, a woman farted on a boy.

clean.tx: ajaɛ̃kɛ kuɾumĩ uʔɪsɛpɛtu iʃapɛ kʷaɾ ɾupi kutuk
clean.tl: Afterwards, the boy pierced her through the anus with a wood-tipped arrow.

clean.tx: taʔɪn ukʷɛɾ ɔu ʔɪ pɪtun ɾahã pamɛ amɛʔɛ̃ aʔi ai pɪnu ɔhɔ ɛhɛ jɛ
clean.tl: Night after night, while a boy was lying , it is said that an old roguish woman came to fart on him.

clean.tx: pɛ pɪtun jɛ tĩ pɛ pɪnu ɔhɔ jɛ tĩ
clean.tl: Each night that came, she farted on him again.

clean.tx: taʔɪn ukʷɛɾta jɛ tĩ kɔ aʔi ihajkɛ piɾɔkhũ jɛ pɛ iʔaɾpɛ pɪnuhũ
clean.tl: When the boy went to sleep again, the old woman took off her skirt, it is said; then farted on him a lot.

clean.tx: pɪnu∼pɪnuatɛ ɛhɛ jɛ
clean.tl: She was really farting a lot on him.

clean.tx: pɛ ɔhɔ jɛ tĩ
clean.tl: She went again .

clean.tx: taʔɪnkɛ itawa imu paɾahɪahɪ ipɛ jɛ
clean.tl: The boy was yellowish , his brother was very angry with him.

clean.tx: nɛtawatɛ nɛkɛã nɛjɪtɪʔɪmtɛ amɔ̃ ʔɪ
clean.tl: “You are yellowish and very lazy too.”

clean.tx: panduʔɪm∼anu taʔɪn jɛ tĩ
clean.tl: The boy didn’t say anything.

clean.tx: pɛ pɪtun jɛ tĩ pɛ aʔi … pɪtun pɪtɛɾpɛ jɛ
clean.tl: Another night, the old … in the middle of the night.

clean.tx: pɛ aʔi ihɔn iʃɔ jɛ ʔɪ
clean.tl: Then the old woman went .

clean.tx: pɛ ihajkɛ musɪɾɪk jɛ pɛ taʔɪn ukʷɛɾatu jɛ pũũũ iapũi ɾɛhɛ pɪnu jɛ
clean.tl: So, she raised her own skirt, the child was sleeping deeply: Puum!

clean.tx: pɛ pɛ wɛɾa uwɪɾ tĩ pɛ imu panu ipɛ mɪja nɛʃɔha tĩ
clean.tl: So … so the light came again, and his brother said: “What’s wrong with you?”

clean.tx: pɛ imu uʔɪ ɾaʔɪr mujã ipɛ jɛ uʔɪ sɛpɛtu ɪɾapaɾ ɾaʔɪɾ
clean.tl: Then, his brother … made a small arrow with a tip of wood and a small bow for him.

clean.tx: pɛ taʔɪn ukʷɛɾ uwɪɾ jɛ tĩ pɪtun ɾahã
clean.tl: The boy went to sleep again, at night.

clean.tx: pɛ aʔi ai tuɾ jɛ tĩ
clean.tl: The old woman came again.

clean.tx: pɛ saʔɛ aʔi ihaj ʃiɾuɾkɛ piɾɔkhũ jɛ ihaj ai jɛ
clean.tl: So he … the old woman raised her own old skirt, her pants.

clean.tx: pɛ saʔɛ uʔɪkɛ hɪkɪj jɛ Sõõ ʃapɛ kʷaɾ ɾupi atɛ jingɔ mɔnɔ jɛ aʔi ai ahɛm atɛ ɔhɔ jɛ
clean.tl: So, he took the arrow and Sõõ!

clean.tx: pɛ aʔɪ ai pɪnu ʔɪm jɛ ʔɪ amɔ̃ kuʔɛm ɾahã saʔɛ amɔ̃ wɛɾa uwɪɾ jɛ ʔɪ
clean.tl: Then, the old woman didn’t fart anymore; the next morning … Another day came.

clean.tx: pɛ pɪtun ɔhɔ tĩ aʔi ju...ju... juwɪɾ ʔɪm ɔhɔ pɪtun ɾahã
clean.tl: So, night came again; the old woman didn’t return.

clean.tx: amõ ukʷɛɾ ɾahã aʔi amɛʔɛ̃ aʔikɛ maʔɛ jɛ ʔɪ
clean.tl: The next day, that old woman got sick.

clean.tx: pɛ sawaʔɛ amɛʔɛ̃ taʔɪnuhu ukʷa je
clean.tl: That young boy already knew.

clean.tx: pɛʔɛ̃ aʔi ihɛ̃ ɾɛhɛ pɪnu iʃɔ ɾikiã amɛʔɛ̃ pɪtun ɾahã
clean.tl: “That old woman was farting on me that night.”

clean.tx: saʔɛkɛ pɛ tujhakɛ
clean.tl: There was the boy.

clean.tx: ɪmantɛ pɛ aʔikɛ manɔ̃ jɛ
clean.tl: Later, the old woman died.

clean.tx: pɛ amɛʔɛ̃ taʔɪn tuʃapɛ panu jɛ
clean.tl: Then, the child talked to the chief:

clean.tx: ihɛ̃ amɛʔɛ̃ aʔikɛ ajukʷa
clean.tl: “I killed that old woman.”

clean.tx: pɛ tuʃa aja ipɛ jɛ
clean.tl: So, the warrior chief said to him:

clean.tx: kawĩ taʔɪnta jahupiɾ ɾahã ɛpanu kɪ̃ hɛtahapɛ
clean.tl: “Beer, when we will lift the children, talk to the people.”

clean.tx: pɛ saʔɛ kapɪpɛ tuj jɛ
clean.tl: He stayed in the room .

clean.tx: pɛ akaju ɾɪkʷɛɾ ŋãʔu jɛ ʔɪ pɛ saʔɛ uhɛm jɛ ʔɪ
clean.tl: Then … Later, after they drank cashew beer, he came out.

clean.tx: kapɪ ĩ uhɛm
clean.tl: He left the seclusion room.

clean.tx: kujãtakɛ upa mupinim
clean.tl: All the women were painted.

clean.tx: aja ɾahã saʔɛ aʔɛ uhɛm taʔɪnuhu taʔɪnuhu jɛ
clean.tl: At this moment, the young man left the room.

clean.tx: maʔɛ huwɪkɛ
clean.tl: And … The blood …

clean.tx: upa tɪmã muʔi huwɪkɛ upa muhãj jɛ
clean.tl: The lower part of his legs was scarified; the blood was totally dispersed.

clean.tx: huwɪ ahɪ–hakɛ aʔi ɾuwɪkɛ amɛʔɛ̃ja saka jɛ
clean.tl: The evil and toxic blood, it was as if it were the blood of the old woman.

clean.tx: pɛ aja ɾahã katu jɛ tĩ
clean.tl: So … In this way he became well again.

clean.tx: pɛ sɔɾɔka ɾɛhɛ wata atu iʃɔ tĩ
clean.tl: And he was able to walk outside again.

flagged.tl: So … So, the arrow broke in her vagina.
